name: Fly.io
summary: Fly.io has no spending cap and, by its own docs, no billing alerts yet, so once a card is on file you pay for whatever you run.
free_tier: New organizations do not get a free tier or a monthly free allowance. New accounts get a small one-time trial credit that lasts 7 days or until it is used up, and no credit card is needed to start. A few things are always free, such as inbound data transfer, shared IPv4, IPv6, some SSL certificates and a small amount of volume snapshot storage. Organizations on plans that were discontinued in October 2024 keep the free allowances from those plans.
over_free_tier: On the trial, when the credit runs out your Machines stay stopped and you cannot start them or create new resources until you add a credit card. Once a card is added, all usage is billed monthly. Fly.io's docs say: "there's no soft ceiling. If you go over, we'll bill you."
hard_cap: No. Fly.io has no spending cap. Prepaid credits do not work as a cap either: a Fly.io staff member wrote in June 2026 that "Credits are not a way to control spend." Credits are used first, and any unpaid balance is charged to the payment method on file.
never_capped: Stopped Machines still cost money for their root file system.
Volumes are billed whether attached, detached, or attached to a stopped Machine.
Dedicated IPv4 addresses and static egress IPs, if you add them.
gotchas: Fly.io's cost management page says: "We don't support billing alerts (yet), so budget accordingly." Check the "current month to date bill" in your dashboard yourself.
Buying prepaid credits does not stop charges. When credits run out, the rest is charged to your card.
Stopping a Machine does not make it free. Delete Machines and volumes you no longer need.
Fly.io's own advice is that auto-stop savings are not guaranteed, so budget for the cost of keeping your Machines always on.
Fly.io says it is willing to discuss refunds if resources were created by mistake or an attack caused an unexpectedly large bill. Email billing@fly.io. This is not guaranteed.
